name: Imageflow
workload: Resizing and re-encoding JPEGs through imageflow_tool or libimageflow (README claim; the benchmark page is on imageflow.io).
claimed_speedup: README: imageflow_tool is 'Up to 17x faster than ImageMagick'. A WebSearch snippet of the imageflow.io benchmark page adds 'about 17x faster than ImageMagick and 2-3x faster than libvips for resizing large jpegs' (snippet only).
tradeoffs: AGPL-3.0 unless a commercial licence is bought; Rust core with a C ABI (four functions needed for bindings), so usable from C++ through that ABI; the repo's recent commits move image codecs to Rust ('zen') crates.
caveats: Snippet only for the benchmark page: www.imageflow.io/benchmarks is blocked in this environment, so methodology, versions and hardware are unconfirmed. The repo's benchmarks folder holds dated codec benchmarks (c-vs-zen-codecs, 2026-04-15, and jpeg-q-ssim2), not a resize shootout against ImageMagick. A recorded independent entry (FastResize) also benchmarks against imageflow 2.0. A libvips issue thread and a sharp issue ask for third-party verification of the 17x figure.
found_via: WebSearch 'imageflow benchmark faster than ImageMagick libvips resize results repository' and the imageflow README.

verification.tier_reason: The README (benchmark_url) carries only the first-party line 'Up to 17x faster than ImageMagick' with no harness, machine or commands; the timed figures exist only on www.imageflow.io/benchmarks, which is blocked here and was read through search snippets, and no ImageMagick/libvips harness exists in the repo (benchmarks/ holds only the 2026-04-15 C-vs-zen codec runs on a Ryzen 9 7950X). First-party, partial methodology, snippet-only numbers: C.
verification.notes: Real, widely used project (4.4k stars, last commit 2026-08-29); metadata confirmed. Language field should read 'Rust with a C ABI (libimageflow; bundles C components)' via a decision override, since verify corrections cannot set language. A paper-free retier needs the imageflow.io benchmarks page or its scripts, which were not found on github.com.
verification.reject_reason: Invalid evidence (MQF precedent, enricher e32 on 2026-10-04): the catalogued 2020 benchmark rows (Imageflow 373.9 ms versus ImageMagick 6555.1 ms and libvips 1002.8 ms, 17.5x and 2.7x) time job launch, not the resize. bench.sh and imageflow-web _pages/benchmarks.md run imageflow_tool under GNU parallel with an unquoted '&', which backgrounds the tool so that hyperfine measures the launch while the tool itself receives only '--command width=200'; reproduced with GNU parallel 20150329 (0.27 s reported while a 2 s stand-in ran). The README's 'up to 17x' traces to a 2016 flow-proto1 prototype gist (0.928 s versus ImageMagick 6.9.3-7 15.837 s and libvips 3.055 s on a Xeon E3-1275 v5), not imageflow_tool, and is not like-for-like (vips --linear disables shrink-on-load, no ImageMagick jpeg:size hint, Imageflow IDCT pre-shrinks); the project's own issue #132 (2017) measured imageflow_tool at 135.24 s against vips 97.09 s. A minor performance bug remains: ir4 get_preshrink_ratio uses from.h / to.w.

name: ucstrcase
workload: Case-insensitive comparison of generated UTF-8 strings, generated ASCII strings and worst-case matching UTF-8 strings (README timing loop; sizes and iteration counts not stated).
claimed_speedup: README: '5x-10x faster than icu::UnicodeString::caseCompare'. Timings: generated UTF-8 225 ms vs 3604 ms for ICU (strcasecmp 368 ms); generated ASCII 194 ms vs 4486 ms (strcasecmp 360 ms); worst-case matching UTF-8 3069 ms vs 12730 ms (strcasecmp 1988 ms). Ratios (derived from page data): about 16x, 23x and 4.1x faster than ICU.
tradeoffs: C library (usable from C++; vcpkg port files are in the ports directory) for caseless UTF-8 comparison using perfect hashing, adapted from Charlie Vieth's strcase (Go). Handles Unicode simple case folding only as implemented by its tables; not a full-collation or normalization-aware comparison. Worst case is about 50% slower than strcasecmp, which ignores non-ASCII.
caveats: README gives timings with no hardware, compiler, flags, workload sizes, ICU version or benchmark source link, so numbers are unverifiable first-party figures. The text's '5x-10x' headline is inconsistent with its own table (ratios from 4.1x to 23x). Only 8 commits, all on one day in July 2024. Category fit is poor: case-insensitive string comparison, not shaping, rasterization or layout; probably belongs with string or Unicode utilities.
found_via: WebSearch 'C++ Unicode library case folding normalization "faster than ICU" "utf8proc" benchmark github'; README fetched via raw.githubusercontent.com and repo and commits pages opened.

verification.tier_reason: First-party README timing table against icu::UnicodeString::caseCompare; the benchmark code is public (test/bench.cpp, CMake target utf8_bench) but no CPU, compiler, flags, ICU version or run count is given, and no committed version of bench.cpp prints the README's section headers, so the published output came from an uncommitted variant. Claim downgraded because the benchmark design inflates the ratios (pointer-equality short-circuit, ICU charged for char*-to-UTF-16 construction, simple vs full case folding).
verification.notes: Numbers match the README exactly, but the benchmark has design flaws that inflate the ratios (self-comparison pointer short-circuit for half the calls, ICU conversion cost inside the loop, simple vs full folding); not invalid enough to reject since the comparisons do real work on the other half of calls, so kept at C with a strong shortcoming. Category for the orchestrator: Unicode text processing (wave 3 unicode-utf8, ICU baseline), not shaping. License MIT verified from LICENSE (a stale Unlicense comment in CMakeLists.txt is template residue); last commit 2024-07-04, stale.
verification.reject_reason: Invalid evidence: bench.cpp times a self-comparison where the ucstrcase side hits the s == t early return (a no-op path, MQF precedent), while ICU is charged the char*-to-UTF-16 UnicodeString construction inside the loop and does full case folding against ucstrcase's simple folding (Unicode 15.0.0); the README section names match no committed bench.cpp, and no CPU, compiler or flags are stated. README numbers (225/3604, 194/4486, 3069/12730 ms) are real but the 16.0x/23.1x/4.1x ratios do not measure equivalent work. Verify batch 30, 2026-10-03.

name: zenwebp
workload: WebP lossless and lossy encode speed and lossy and lossless decode speed in single-threaded zenbench A/B runs against libwebp (webp 0.3.1 / libwebp-sys 0.14) on a 14-image corpus (CLIC2025 photos, screenshots, CID22).
claimed_speedup: README: lossless encoder method 6 is 2.6x faster than libwebp at 1.01x size (132 ms vs 340 ms on a 512x512 photo, docs/PERFORMANCE.md); lossy encoder method 4 is 1.35x faster at 1.01x size; lossy decode 1.09 to 1.12x faster on 2K photos and 1.06 to 1.14x on screenshots; lossless decode 1.23 to 1.31x on screenshots. Lossless methods 2 to 4 are near parity (1.03x).
compiler_and_flags: cargo bench, default target, no -C target-cpu=native, runtime SIMD dispatch; rustc version not stated
tradeoffs: AGPL-3.0 or paid commercial licence. Pure Rust, no_std capable, bit-exact lossy decoder vs libwebp (0 pixel diffs on 12,825 files per README). Lossless method 0 is 2.4x slower than libwebp. Files within 1 to 5% of libwebp's size.
caveats: Internal contradiction: docs/PERFORMANCE.md (dated 2026-03-26) lists lossy decode as 1.14 to 2.22x SLOWER than libwebp (e.g. 223 vs 496 MPix/s on a 4K screenshot), while the newer README claims 1.06 to 1.14x faster; the README numbers may postdate a rewrite but this is not verified. No CPU model is stated in the files read. Only the lossless encoder method 6 win is consistent across both pages. First-party benchmark.
found_via: Google Scholar / arXiv / ACM DL / IEEE: web search 'imazen zenjpeg zenpng zenwebp faster than libjpeg-turbo libwebp libpng benchmark'

verification.tier_reason: First-party zenbench and callgrind numbers against libwebp (via webp 0.3.1 / libwebp-sys 0.14) with no CPU model or rustc version; the project's own committed data shows zenwebp slower than libwebp in nearly every mode, and its one large 'win' (lossless m6 2.6x) is documented in its own CLAUDE.md as skipped work.
verification.notes: Reject not-faster, and the lone headline win (lossless m6 2.6x) is invalid evidence by the project's own account (it skipped libwebp's predictor-bits search and dual no-cache refs). If kept under keep-and-document, it belongs as a safe-Rust/memory-bounded codec at roughly 0.7 to 0.97x libwebp speed. Rust entry under a C++-filtered category: language-filter mismatch.
verification.reject_reason: Invalid evidence: the README's 'm6 2.6x faster' lossy-encode claim was measured on an incomplete encoder that skipped work (predictor-bits search and dual no-cache references unported before 2026-07-14); the repo's own speed_parity_2026-07-16.md and msweep_post70 TSV show zenwebp slower than libwebp in lossy encode (m4 1.16x, m6 1.40x slower; m2 0.97x the lone win), lossless encode (geomean 1.18-1.92x slower), lossy decode and lossless decode. Derived from image-rs/image-webp. Verify batch 20, 2026-10-03.

name: av2-turbo (AVM SYCL GPU acceleration)
baseline: AVM (AV2 reference encoder) CPU code paths; the benchmark table calls it only 'CPU Baseline' with no encoder, version or flags named
workload: SYCL/CUDA/OpenCL GPU kernels for DCT 8x8, SAD 16x16 motion estimation, loop filter and intra prediction, plus a 'full encoding pipeline' fps table at 720p, 1080p and 4K.
claimed_speedup: README: '3-5x real-world speedup on AV2 encoding'. docs/benchmarks.md: 1080p30 124 fps on RTX 4090 vs 28 fps 'CPU Baseline' (4.4x); 4K30 38 fps vs 8 fps (4.8x); 720p30 185 fps vs 45 fps (4.1x). Kernel rows: DCT 8x8 13.9x-31.4x, SAD 16x16 17.1x-24.0x, loop filter 11.1x-11.8x, intra 8x8 11.4x-12.0x.
compiler_and_flags: Intel DPC++ 2024.0, GCC 11.4, CUDA 12.2, NVIDIA driver 535.154.05, CMake Release build
hardware: Config A: Intel i9-13900K + NVIDIA RTX 4090 (24 GB); Config B: i7-12700K + RTX 3080; Config C: i7-12700K + Arc A770; Config D: Ryzen 9 7950X + RX 7900 XTX
tradeoffs: Needs a GPU and a SYCL toolchain (DPC++ or AdaptiveCpp). Batching is required because single-kernel launch overhead is 94% of a single DCT 8x8. AMD and ARM backends are marked in progress. License follows the AVM codebase (BSD 3-Clause Clear with the AOMedia patent license).
caveats: Very low confidence in the claim. The repository holds only SYCL kernels and wrappers, not an encoder, so the 'full encoding pipeline' fps figures cannot come from the repo's own code. The visible test results in the README are unit-test timings (for example DCT 8x8 average 50.14 us on an Intel Xeon Gold 6530 with OpenCL), not encoder runs. The CPU baseline is unnamed, no raw logs, CSV or CI output are published, and the fps figures look implausibly high for an AV2 reference-class encoder. No end-to-end comparison against an unmodified AVM encoder is given. Tier C only because numbers exist without a stated methodology; the verifier should check whether the data is real.
found_via: WebFetch of github.com/topics/hevc?l=c%2B%2B and topics/av1?l=c%2B%2B (only repo flagged with a speed claim), then WebSearch 'av2-turbo github AV2 encoder decoder faster than libaom benchmark'

verification.tier_reason: docs/benchmarks.md does contain the fps and kernel tables quoted in the record. Its only baseline is an unnamed 'CPU Baseline' (no AVM version, encoder settings or CPU named for that column). No code in the repo can produce those tables. tests/sycl_perf_test.cpp's main() only calls InitGoogleTest/RUN_ALL_TESTS, so the documented '--benchmark --iterations=1000 --warmup=100' and '--csv=results.csv' flags do not exist. Its CPU-vs-SYCL test, DISABLED_TransformPerformance, is disabled, and its 'SYCL' loop calls av2_fwd_txfm2d_c on the CPU ('placeholder - uses CPU for now', 'TODO: Replace with actual SYCL kernel'). The repo has no SAD, loop-filter or intra CPU-vs-GPU benchmark, and no encoder at all.
verification.notes: Reject for invalid evidence, as the search agent suspected: the tables look fabricated or are at least unsupported by any code or log in the repo, and the repo's only real test log contradicts them. If the keep-and-document rule is applied anyway, cap at D, usability reference (BSD-3-Clause-Clear) and has_code false for the claimed encoder. Metadata checked: 8 stars, 0 forks, 29 commits, last commit 2026-04-04, not a fork. The README badges point at hbliu007/avm-sycl-gpu-acceleration, which appears to be the repo's former name.
verification.reject_reason: Invalid evidence: the repo holds no encoder; the documented --benchmark and --csv flags do not exist in tests/sycl_perf_test.cpp, the only CPU-vs-SYCL test (DISABLED_TransformPerformance) is disabled and times the CPU av2_fwd_txfm2d_c twice ('placeholder - uses CPU for now'), and its own docs/TEST_REPORT.md says the GPU backend was not tested (Xeon Gold 6530, OpenCL CPU). The claimed AVM speedups cannot have been measured from this code. Verify batch 45, 2026-10-03.
